newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan OKs plan to lift overseas stock futures ban.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan OKs plan to lift overseas stock futures ban.

text.p: Taiwan's Finance Minister Paul Chiu had approved a proposal to lift a ban on local trading of offshore Taiwan stock-index futures in Chicago and Singapore, a ministry official said on Wednesday.
"As Minister Chiu had promised previously to approve lifting the ban by end-April, he approved the proposal on Tuesday," the official said by telephone.
"Our ministry will submit the proposal to the cabinet for final approval as soon as possible," she said.

Under the liberalisation, Taiwan futures houses for the first time will be able to trade futures linked to Taiwan stock market performance offered by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange and Singapore International Monetary Exchange.

The CME and SIMEX launched the contracts on January 9 over the objections of Taiwan market regulators, who had pleaded in vain for them to wait until Taipei could open its own futures market and launch its own stock index contracts.

Under a Futures Trading Law enacted by parliament in early March after years of bickering and delays, the exchange can open no sooner than October -- giving the SIMEX and CME at least a several-month window of opportunity to attract Taiwan customers.
Singapore traders and analysts had said the SIMEX would benefit most from Taiwan's liberalisation. The CME, however, did not give comments immediately. -- Taipei Newsroom (5080815)
